precepts.text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
precepts.point: Servants have ruled over us. The statue of Roosevelt on horseback with a Native and an African man walking beside him shows it.

note.label: Latinos For Trump: Alien Vs. Predator

precepts.why:
“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand”. Who is ruling over us? Servants. The Most High made Esau to serve us, but we are serving them now.

Look at the statue they took down: Theodore Roosevelt on horseback, with a Native man and an African man walking beside him. They took it down, but it is too late; they know who they are and they know who we are. Roosevelt represents Esau, the servant. Now watch the scripture come to life: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth”. The horse represents authority, power and rulership. The princes walking on foot are Israel, the northern kingdom on the left and the southern kingdom on the right, walking as servants.

Esau knows who he is, and he knows this is his time to rule. But it is coming to an end. There is none that can deliver us out of their hand, not Hugo Chavez, not Fidel Castro, not Maduro with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware. No man can save us. Our power is to keep God's commandments in the faith of Christ; when we do that, the Most High and his angels will fight for us. We have to see ourselves in these scriptures, no longer as blacks or as Latinos, but as one people, one nation.

precepts.text: Curse not the king in thy thought, for a bird of the air shall carry the voice.
precepts.point: God brings every work into judgment with every secret thing, good or evil.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

precepts.text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
precepts.point: Their Redeemer is strong and will plead their cause and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
Israel is a people robbed and spoiled, and spoiled means severely damaged or harmed in a way that reduces value, marred or ruined. Solomon gives the picture of it: “There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.”

Folly is set in great dignity: the foolish things, the vessels of wrath, raised up high. And the rich sit in low place: the real rich, the ones the Lord speaks to in Revelation, knowing their poverty and their sufferings, yet calling them rich. Israel is rich, yet sits low.

“I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.” Those who were meant to serve us are in positions of authority and high value, and the princes, the sons of God, walk as servants upon the earth. If that's not the visual for spoiled when you read robbed and spoiled, nothing is.

That is the oppression of Jeremiah 50:33: Israel and Judah held fast by those who took them captive. And that is why none can restore it but the Redeemer who will plead their cause and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.

precepts.text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth, so the rest from war was spent building up, not idling.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.”

Rest is not idleness. Asa “had no war in those years; because the Lord had given him rest”, and he spent that rest building up, not idling: walls, towers, gates, and bars, “while the land is yet before us.” “So they built and prospered.”

points: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun: the Most High showed him the visions of where this planet is going. As an error which proceedeth from the ruler: meaning the wrong people are ruling. The wrong type of rulership is on this planet now.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'
